overall: The Council violated the Open Meeting Law by not providing real-time access to part of its October 13 meeting; the committees' September notice and Facebook complaints were not violations. Minutes revision was recommended, not ordered.

allegations.summary: A committee member allegedly posted confusing Facebook information saying an August 27 committee meeting could be viewed via Zoom, when the official notice said ECTV.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee on Legislative Affairs and Elections did not violate the Law.

allegations.summary: Allegation that the Director of Communications for Everett Community Television violated the Open Meeting Law by the Facebook post.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review any allegation that the Director violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee of the Whole on Budget's September 19 agenda allegedly included an extraneous page about a May 2018 School Department hearing, with outdated School Committee information.
allegations.key_passage: We agree that the final page referring to a May 2018 hearing, although confusing, seems to have been in error;

allegations.summary: Allegations concerning the City Clerk's conduct related to the meetings.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons noted above, we decline to review any allegation that the City Clerk violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Allegations about who was invited to attend or speak at the meeting, and that the Chair praised the City and City Clerk.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations, even if true, do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Portions of the Council's October 13 meeting were not broadcast live due to technical problems, so the public could not follow those portions in real time.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law where the Council did not provide real-time access to a portion of its October 13 meeting.

allegations.summary: General allegation that the Council's meetings have had technical problems making them inaccessible for several months.
allegations.key_passage: Complainants must allege violations with a degree of specificity, as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainant: the September 19 budget hearing notice did not clearly say whether the public could attend in person or only via ECTV. Raised by the AG on its own.
allegations.key_passage: If the public was permitted to attend the meeting in person, the meeting notice should have included the street address of the meeting location.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainant: minutes of the September 16 and 19 budget hearings lacked times, attendance, discussion summaries and exhibit lists. Raised by the AG on its own.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes do not include the time of the meetings, do not include a list of members present or absent, do not include a summary of the discussions held on each matter, and do not include a list of documents and other exhibits used at the meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
